concern: Withholding the XXY screen's clean negative for an unresolvable X dosage
scope_of_claims: This change WITHHOLDS an affirmative negative. It asserts no positive finding, introduces no threshold and moves none — the only constant change makes an already-calibrated bound visible to a second module. Exactly one background fact is load-bearing and is evidenced below with primary sources. Everything else in the diff is software behaviour, verifiable from the code and its tests.

C1.statement: The 47,XXY (Klinefelter) karyotype is a supernumerary X on a Y-bearing karyotype — the pattern requires a Y chromosome.
C1.load_bearing_for: Why the new escalation is conditional on a chrY signal (`ambiguous_x and y_discordant`) rather than unconditional: with no chrY signal an unresolved X dosage has nothing to pair with, so this change leaves the screen's existing answer there untouched. C1 does NOT establish, and this packet does not claim, that an evaluable chrY rate at or below THRESHOLD_Y_PAR_NOISE means no Y is present on a consumer array -- see pre_existing_behaviour.
C1.independence: Disjoint authors, 16 years apart, different study designs (single-case cytogenetic description vs consecutive-newborn survey) and different cohorts (UK clinical case vs 14,069 Canadian newborns). Neither derives from the other's data.

x_dosage_zones.statement: That a non-PAR X-heterozygosity RATE separates one X from two X, and that a rate between the calibrated bounds is unresolved, is pre-existing behaviour of backend/services/sex_inference.py. This change does not introduce, alter or re-derive it — it makes the existing lower bound importable so the screen can see the same three zones the classifier already used.
x_dosage_zones.existing_in_repo_citation: PMID:28035028 (cited in four places in the codebase before this change)
x_dosage_zones.note: Recorded here for traceability, NOT claimed as newly evidenced by this packet. It is deliberately not run through the two-source gate, because this change makes no new assertion about it. Re-deriving the thresholds would be its own issue.

y_noise_floor.statement: Whether an evaluable chrY non-no-call rate at or below THRESHOLD_Y_PAR_NOISE (0.10) is 'no Y signal' on a consumer array is the sex classifier's calibrated PAR-noise floor, shared with the screen since #1130 and documented in docs/internal/sex_inference_threshold_validation.md. This change neither introduces, moves nor re-derives it, and this packet does not re-assert it: the ambiguous-X / no-Y-signal arm keeps exactly the answer the screen gave before. If that calibration is wrong, the negative it produces was wrong before this change and is exactly as wrong after it.
y_noise_floor.correction: An earlier revision of this README used C1 (the karyotype definition) as if it justified the negative at that measurement boundary. A karyotype definition cannot establish an array threshold's sensitivity; the sentence was withdrawn on 2026-09-05 after review and the arm is recorded as unchanged pre-existing behaviour instead.

explicitly_not_claimed: The issue's own evidence gate discusses mosaic 46,XY/47,XXY and the relationship between X-het and aneuploid-cell fraction. None of that is asserted or evidenced here, because an unresolved X dosage is withheld rather than interpreted. Earlier revisions of the pull request carried an intermediate-chromosome-complement mechanism, a FISH confirmation recommendation, and a statement about what X heterozygosity measures; all three were removed rather than evidenced, and a test now enforces that none returns to the patient-facing text.

payload_integrity: Five payloads are unedited verbatim NCBI responses (two eSummary, three eLink). One payload, the NCBI EFetch XML for the three cited PMIDs, is SANITIZED: <Abstract> elements were removed under the bibliographic-metadata-only retention rule and nothing else was touched; it is labelled as such in its filename. Four payloads are DERIVED records labelled as such in the file itself: the Consensus call and the two Scite calls, none of which has an HTTP response to capture, and the reduction of the EFetch XML to its CommentsCorrections and publication-type fields. No payload required further sanitization: all are public bibliographic records with no genotype, sample, personal or credentialed data.

retraction_method: PubMed EFetch XML read for typed CommentsCorrections relations (RefType), not publication type and not eLink. An original record keeps its own pubtype while corrections, errata and retractions are carried as separate linked records. The eLink `pubmed_pubmed*` link sets retained here are generic related-article neighbourhoods and do not expose the typed relation -- an earlier revision treated their silence as clearance, which it is not. The typed check was run 2026-09-05 for all three cited PMIDs; the sanitized XML is the authority and raw/ncbi-pubmed-comments-corrections-derived.json is its reduction.
